R137|base|4.1.heading: Approval
R137|base|4.1.text: If the vehicle type submitted for approval pursuant to this Regulation meets the requirements of this Regulation, approval of that vehicle type shall be granted.

R137|base|4.1.1.heading: Approval
R137|base|4.1.1.text: The Technical Service appointed in accordance with paragraph 12. below shall check whether the required conditions have been satisfied.

R137|base|4.1.2.heading: Approval
R137|base|4.1.2.text: In case of doubt, account shall be taken, when verifying the conformity of the vehicle to the requirements of this Regulation, of any data or test results provided by the manufacturer which can be taken into consideration in validating the approval test carried out by the Technical Service.

R137|base|4.2.heading: Approval
R137|base|4.2.text: An approval number shall be assigned to each type approved in accordance with Schedule 4 of the Agreement (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).

R137|base|4.3.heading: Approval
R137|base|4.3.text: Notice of approval or of refusal of approval of a vehicle type pursuant to this Regulation shall be communicated by the Parties to the Agreement which apply this Regulation by means of a form conforming to the model in Annex 1 to this Regulation.

R137|base|4.4.heading: Approval
R137|base|4.4.text: There shall be affixed, conspicuously and in a readily accessible place specified on the approval form, to every vehicle conforming to a vehicle type approved under this Regulation, an international approval mark consisting of:

R137|base|4.4.1.heading: Approval
R137|base|4.4.1.text: A circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval;2 2The distinguishing numbers of the Contracting Parties to the 1958 Agreement are reproduced as defined in the Consolidated Resolution on the Construction of Vehicles (R.E.3.), documentECE/TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.7, para. 2 - https://unece.org/transport/standards/transport/vehicleregulations-wp29/resolutions

R137|base|4.4.2.heading: Approval
R137|base|4.4.2.text: The number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, to the right of the circle prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1. above.

R137|base|4.5.heading: Approval
R137|base|4.5.text: If the vehicle conforms to a vehicle type approved, under one or more other Regulations annexed to the Agreement, in the country which has granted approval under this Regulation, the symbol prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1. above need not be repeated; in such a case the Regulation and approval numbers and the additional symbols of all the Regulations under which approval has been granted in the country which has granted approval under this Regulation shall be placed in vertical columns to the right of the symbol prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1.

R137|base|4.6.heading: Approval
R137|base|4.6.text: The approval mark shall be clearly legible and be indelible.

R137|base|4.7.heading: Approval
R137|base|4.7.text: The approval mark shall be placed close to or on the vehicle data plate affixed by the manufacturer.

R137|base|4.8.heading: Approval
R137|base|4.8.text: Annex 2 to this Regulation gives examples of the arrangements of approval marks.

R137|base|Annex 10 1.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity
R137|base|Annex 10 1.text: Purpose Determination of compliance with the requirements of paragraph 5.2.7. of this Regulation.

R137|base|Annex 10 2.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity
R137|base|Annex 10 2.text: Definitions For the purposes of this Annex:

R137|base|Annex 10 2.1.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity
R137|base|Annex 10 2.1.text: " _Enclosed spaces"_ means the special volumes within the vehicle (or the vehicle outline across openings) that are external to the hydrogen system (storage system, fuel cell system, internal combustion engine (ICE) and fuel flow management system).

R137|base|Annex 10 2.2.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity
R137|base|Annex 10 2.2.text: " _Luggage compartment"_ means the space in the vehicle for luggage and/or goods accommodation, bounded by the roof, hood, floor, side walls, being separated from the passenger compartment by the front bulkhead or the rear bulkhead.

R137|base|Annex 10 2.3.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity
R137|base|Annex 10 2.3.text: " _Nominal working pressure (NWP)"_ means the gauge pressure that characterizes typical operation of a system. For compressed hydrogen gas containers, NWP is the settled pressure of compressed gas in a fully fuelled container or storage system at a uniform temperature of 15 °C.

R137|base|Annex 10 3.title: Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions
R137|base|Annex 10 3.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity

R137|base|Annex 10 3.1.title: Compressed hydrogen storage systems and downstream piping
R137|base|Annex 10 3.1.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions
R137|base|Annex 10 3.1.text: Compressed hydrogen storage systems and downstream piping

R137|base|Annex 10 3.1.1.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions > Compressed hydrogen storage systems and downstream piping
R137|base|Annex 10 3.1.1.text: Prior to conducting the crash test, instrumentation is installed in the hydrogen storage system to perform the required pressure and temperature measurements if the standard vehicle does not already possess instrumentation with the required accuracy.

R137|base|Annex 10 3.1.2.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions > Compressed hydrogen storage systems and downstream piping
R137|base|Annex 10 3.1.2.text: The hydrogen storage system is then purged, if necessary, following manufacturer directions to remove impurities from the container before filling the storage system with compressed hydrogen or helium gas. Since the storage system pressure varies with temperature, the targeted fill pressure is a function of the temperature. The target pressure shall be determined from the following equation: Ptarget = NWP x (273 + To) / 288 where NWP is the nominal working pressure (MPa), To is the ambient temperature to which the storage system is expected to settle, and Ptarget is the targeted fill pressure after the temperature settles.

R137|base|Annex 10 3.1.3.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions > Compressed hydrogen storage systems and downstream piping
R137|base|Annex 10 3.1.3.text: The container is filled to a minimum of 95 per cent of the targeted fill pressure and allowed to settle (stabilize) prior to conducting the crash test.

R137|base|Annex 10 3.1.4.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions > Compressed hydrogen storage systems and downstream piping
R137|base|Annex 10 3.1.4.text: The main stop valve and shut-off valves for hydrogen gas, located in the downstream hydrogen gas piping, are in the normal driving condition kept open immediately prior to the impact.

R137|base|Annex 10 3.2.title: Enclosed spaces
R137|base|Annex 10 3.2.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions

R137|base|Annex 10 3.2.1.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions > Enclosed spaces
R137|base|Annex 10 3.2.1.text: Sensors are selected to measure either the build-up of the hydrogen or helium gas or the reduction in oxygen (due to displacement of air by leaking hydrogen/helium).

R137|base|Annex 10 3.2.2.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions > Enclosed spaces
R137|base|Annex 10 3.2.2.text: Sensors are calibrated to traceable references to ensure an accuracy of ±5 per cent at the targeted criteria of 4 per cent hydrogen or 3 per cent helium by volume in air, and a full scale measurement capability of at least 25 per cent above the target criteria. The sensor shall be capable of a 90 per cent response to a full scale change in concentration within 10 seconds.

R137|base|Annex 10 3.2.3.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions > Enclosed spaces
R137|base|Annex 10 3.2.3.text: Prior to the crash impact, the sensors are located in the passenger and luggage compartments of the vehicle as follows: (a) At a distance within 250 mm of the headliner above the driver's seat or near the top centre of the passenger compartment; (b) At a distance within 250 mm of the floor in front of the rear (or rear most) seat in the passenger compartment; and (c) At a distance within 100 mm of the top of luggage compartments inside the vehicle that are not directly affected by the particular crash impact to be conducted.

R137|base|Annex 10 3.2.4.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions > Enclosed spaces
R137|base|Annex 10 3.2.4.text: The sensors are securely mounted on the vehicle structure or seats and protected for the planned crash test from debris, air bag exhaust gas and projectiles. The measurements following the crash are recorded by instruments located in the vehicle or by remote transmission.

R137|base|Annex 10 3.2.5.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions > Enclosed spaces
R137|base|Annex 10 3.2.5.text: The test may be conducted either outdoors in an area protected from the wind and possible solar effects, or indoors in a space that is large enough or ventilated to prevent the build-up of hydrogen to more than 10 per cent of the targeted criteria in the passenger and luggage compartments.

R137|base|Annex 10 4.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity
R137|base|Annex 10 4.text: Post-crash Leak Test Measurement for a Compressed Hydrogen Storage System Filled with Compressed Hydrogen

R137|base|Annex 10 4.1.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions
R137|base|Annex 10 4.1.text: The hydrogen gas pressure, P0 (MPa), and temperature, T0 (°C), are measured immediately before the impact and then at a time interval, Δt (min), after the impact.

R137|base|Annex 10 4.1.1.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions > Enclosed spaces
R137|base|Annex 10 4.1.1.text: The time interval, Δt, starts when the vehicle comes to rest after the impact and continues for at least 60 minutes.

R137|base|Annex 10 4.1.2.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions > Enclosed spaces
R137|base|Annex 10 4.1.2.text: The time interval, Δt shall be increased if necessary in order to accommodate measurement accuracy for a storage system with a large volume operating up to 70MPa; in that case, Δt can be calculated from the following formula: Δt = VCHSS x NWP /1,000 x ((-0.027 x NWP +4) x Rs – 0.21) -1.7 x Rs where Rs = Ps / NWP, Ps is the pressure range of the pressure sensor (MPa), NWP is the Nominal Working Pressure (MPa), VCHSS is the volume of the compressed hydrogen storage system (L), and Δt is the time interval (min).

R137|base|Annex 10 4.1.3.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions > Enclosed spaces
R137|base|Annex 10 4.1.3.text: If the calculated value of Δt is less than 60 minutes, Δt is set to 60 minutes.

R137|base|Annex 10 4.2.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions
R137|base|Annex 10 4.2.text: The initial mass of hydrogen in the storage system can be calculated as follows: Po' = Po x 288 / (273 + T0) ρo' = –0.0027 x (P0')2 + 0.75 x P0' + 1.07 Mo = ρo' x VCHSS

R137|base|Annex 10 4.3.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions
R137|base|Annex 10 4.3.text: Correspondingly, the final mass of hydrogen in the storage system, Mf, at the end of the time interval, Δt, can be calculated as follows: Pf' = Pf x 288 / (273 + Tf) ρf' = –0.0027 x (Pf')2 + 0.75 x Pf' + 1.07 Mf = ρf' x VCHSS where Pf is the measured final pressure (MPa) at the end of the time interval, and Tf is the measured final temperature (°C).

R137|base|Annex 10 4.4.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions
R137|base|Annex 10 4.4.text: The average hydrogen flow rate over the time interval is therefore: VH2 = (Mf-Mo) / Δt x 22.41 / 2.016 x (Ptarget /Po) where VH2 is the average volumetric flow rate (NL/min) over the time interval and the term (Ptarget/Po) is used to compensate for differences between the measured initial pressure (Po) and the targeted fill pressure (Ptarget).

R137|base|Annex 10 5.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity
R137|base|Annex 10 5.text: Post-Crash Leak Test Measurement for a Compressed Hydrogen Storage System Filled with Compressed Helium

R137|base|Annex 10 5.1.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions
R137|base|Annex 10 5.1.text: The helium gas pressure, P0 (MPa), and temperature T0 (°C), are measured immediately before the impact and then at a predetermined time interval after the impact.

R137|base|Annex 10 5.1.1.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions > Enclosed spaces
R137|base|Annex 10 5.1.1.text: The time interval, Δt, starts when the vehicle comes to rest after the impact and continues for at least 60 minutes.

R137|base|Annex 10 5.1.2.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions > Enclosed spaces
R137|base|Annex 10 5.1.2.text: The time interval, Δt, shall be increased, if necessary, in order to accommodate measurement accuracy for a storage system with a large volume operating up to 70 MPa; in that case, Δt can be calculated from the following equation: Δt = VCHSS x NWP /1000 x ((-0.028 x NWP +5.5) x Rs – 0.3) – 2.6 x Rs where Rs = Ps / NWP, Ps is the pressure range of the pressure sensor (MPa), NWP is the Nominal Working Pressure (MPa), VCHSS is the volume of the compressed storage system (L), and Δt is the time interval (min).

R137|base|Annex 10 5.1.3.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions > Enclosed spaces
R137|base|Annex 10 5.1.3.text: If the value of Δt is less than 60 minutes, Δt is set to 60 minutes.

R137|base|Annex 10 5.2.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions
R137|base|Annex 10 5.2.text: The initial mass of helium in the storage system is calculated as follows: Po' = Po x 288 / (273 + T0) ρo' = –0.0043 x (P0')2 + 1.53 x P0' + 1.49 Mo = ρo' x VCHSS

R137|base|Annex 10 5.3.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions
R137|base|Annex 10 5.3.text: The final mass of helium in the storage system at the end of the time interval, Δt, is calculated as follows: Pf' = Pf x 288 / (273 + Tf) ρf' = –0.0043 x (Pf')2 + 1.53 x Pf' + 1.49 Mf = ρf' x VCHSS where Pf is the measured final pressure (MPa) at the end of the time interval, and Tf is the measured final temperature (°C).

R137|base|Annex 10 5.4.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions
R137|base|Annex 10 5.4.text: The average helium flow rate over the time interval is therefore: VHe = (Mf-Mo) / Δt x 22.41 / 4.003 x (Ptarget/ Po) where VHe is the average volumetric flow rate (NL/min) over the time interval and the term (Ptarget/Po) is used to compensate for differences between the measured initial pressure (Po) and the targeted fill pressure (Ptarget).

R137|base|Annex 10 5.5.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Preparation, Instrumentation and Test Conditions
R137|base|Annex 10 5.5.text: Conversion of the average volumetric flow of helium to the average hydrogen flow is calculated with the following formula: VH2 = VHe / 0.75 where VH2 is the corresponding average volumetric flow of hydrogen.

R137|base|Annex 10 6.title: Post-Crash Concentration Measurement for Enclosed Spaces
R137|base|Annex 10 6.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity
R137|base|Annex 10 6.text: Post-Crash Concentration Measurement for Enclosed Spaces

R137|base|Annex 10 6.1.heading: Annex 10 Test Conditions and Procedures for the Assessment of Post-Crash Hydrogen Fuel System Integrity > Post-Crash Concentration Measurement for Enclosed Spaces
R137|base|Annex 10 6.1.text: Post-crash data collection in enclosed spaces commences when the vehicle comes to a rest. Data from the sensors installed in accordance with paragraph 3.2. of this annex are collected at least every five seconds and continue for a period of 60 minutes after the test. A first-order lag (time constant) up to a maximum of five seconds may be applied to the measurements to provide "smoothing" and filter the effects of spurious data points. Specifications for the restraint system test (Full Width Rigid Barrier test) In the case of a compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle, compliance with paragraphs 5.2.7.1. to 5.2.7.3. shall be shown.

R137|base|Annex 9 0.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train
R137|base|Annex 9 0.text: This annex describes test procedures to demonstrate compliance to the electrical safety requirements of paragraph 5.2.8. of this Regulation.

R137|base|Annex 9 1.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train
R137|base|Annex 9 1.text: Test setup and equipment If a high voltage disconnect function is used, measurements are to be taken from both sides of the device performing the disconnect function. However, if the high voltage disconnect is integral to the REESS or the energy conversion system and the high-voltage bus of the REESS or the energy conversion system is protected according to protection IPXXB following the impact test, measurements may only be taken between the device performing the disconnect function and the electrical loads. The voltmeter used in this test shall measure DC values and have an internal resistance of at least 10 MΩ.

R137|base|Annex 9 2.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train
R137|base|Annex 9 2.text: The following instructions may be used if voltage is measured. After the impact test, determine the high voltage bus voltages (Ub, U1, U2) (see Figure 1 below). The voltage measurement shall be made not earlier than 10 seconds, but, not later than 60 seconds after the impact. This procedure is not applicable if the test is performed under the condition where the electric power train is not energized. Figure 1 **Measurement of Ub, U1, U2**

R137|base|Annex 9 3.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train
R137|base|Annex 9 3.text: Assessment procedure for low electrical energy Prior to the impact a switch S1 and a known discharge resistor Re is connected in parallel to the relevant capacitance (ref. Figure 2 below). (a) Not earlier than 10 seconds and not later than 60 seconds after the impact the switch S1 shall be closed while the voltage Ub and the current Ie are measured and recorded. The product of the voltage Ub and the current Ie shall be integrated over the period of time, starting from the moment when the switch S1 is closed (tc) until the voltage Ub falls below the high voltage threshold of 60 V DC (th). The resulting integration equals the Total Energy (TE) in joules. (b) When Ub is measured at a point in time between 10 seconds and 60 seconds after the impact and the capacitance of the X-capacitors (Cx) is specified by the manufacturer, Total Energy (TE) shall be calculated according to the following formula: 2 TE = 0.5 x Cx x Ub (c) WhenU1 and U2 (see Figure 1 above) are measured at a point in time between 10 seconds and 60 seconds after the impact and the capacitances of the Y-capacitors (Cy1, Cy2) are specified by the manufacturer, Total Energy (TEy1, TEy2) shall be calculated according to the following formulas: 2 TEy1 = 0.5 x Cy1 x U1 2 TEy2 = 0.5 x Cy2 x U2 This procedure is not applicable if the test is performed under the condition where the electric power train is not energized. Figure 2 **E.g. measurement of high voltage bus energy stored in X-capacitors**

R137|base|Annex 9 4.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train
R137|base|Annex 9 4.text: Physical protection Following the vehicle impact test any parts surrounding the high voltage components shall be, without the use of tools, opened, disassembled or removed. All remaining surrounding parts shall be considered part of the physical protection. The jointed test finger described in Figure 3 shall be inserted into any gaps or openings of the physical protection with a test force of 10 N ± 10 per cent for electrical safety assessment. If partial or full penetration into the physical protection by the jointed test finger occurs, the jointed test finger shall be placed in every position as specified below. Starting from the straight position, both joints of the test finger shall be rotated progressively through an angle of up to 90 degrees with respect to the axis of the adjoining section of the finger and shall be placed in every possible position. Internal electrical protection barriers are considered part of the enclosure If appropriate a low-voltage supply (of not less than 40 V and not more than 50 V) in series with a suitable lamp should be connected, between the jointed test finger and high voltage live parts inside the electrical protection barrier or enclosure. Figure 3 **Jointed Test Finger** Material: metal, except where otherwise specified Linear dimensions in mm. Tolerances on dimensions without specific tolerance: (a) on angles: +0/-10 seconds; (b) on linear dimensions: (i) up to 25 mm: +0/-0.05; (ii) over 25 mm: ±0.2. Both joints shall permit movement in the same plane and the same direction through an angle of 90° with a 0 to +10° tolerance. The requirements of paragraph 5.2.8.1.3. of this Regulation are met if the jointed test finger described in Figure 3, is unable to contact high voltage live parts. If necessary a mirror or a fiberscope may be used in order to inspect whether the jointed test finger touches the high voltage buses. If this requirement is verified by a signal circuit between the jointed test finger and high voltage live parts, the lamp shall not light.

R137|base|Annex 9 4.1.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train
R137|base|Annex 9 4.1.text: Test method for measuring electric resistance: (a) Test method using a resistance tester. The resistance tester is connected to the measuring points (typically, electrical chassis and electro conductive enclosure/electrical protection barrier) and the resistance is measured using a resistance tester that meets the specification that follows: (i) Resistance tester: Measurement current at least 0.2 A; (ii) Resolution: 0.01 Ω or less; (iii) The resistance R shall be less than 0.1 Ω. (b) Test method using DC power supply, voltmeter and ammeter. The DC power supply, voltmeter and ammeter are connected to the measuring points (Typically, electrical chassis and electro conductive enclosure/electrical protection barrier). The voltage of the DC power supply is adjusted so that the current flow becomes at least 0.2 A. The current "I" and the voltage "U" are measured. The resistance "R" is calculated according to the following formula: R = U / I The resistance R shall be less than 0.1 Ω. Note: If lead wires are used for voltage and current measurement, each lead wire shall be independently connected to the electrical protection barrier/enclosure/electrical chassis. Terminal can be common for voltage measurement and current measurement. Example of the test method using DC power supply, voltmeter and ammeter is shown below. Figure 4 **Example of theTest Method using DC Power Supply**

R137|base|Annex 9 5.title: Isolation resistance
R137|base|Annex 9 5.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train

R137|base|Annex 9 5.1.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train > Isolation resistance
R137|base|Annex 9 5.1.text: General The isolation resistance for each high voltage bus of the vehicle is measured or shall be determined by calculating the measurement values of each part or component unit of a high voltage bus. All measurements for calculating voltage(s) and electrical isolation are made after a minimum of 10 seconds after the impact.

R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train > Isolation resistance
R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.text: Measurement method The isolation resistance measurement is conducted by selecting an appropriate measurement method from among those listed in paragraphs 5.2.1. to 5.2.2. of this Annex, depending on the electrical charge of the live parts or the isolation resistance. The range of the electrical circuit to be measured is clarified in advance, using electrical circuit diagrams. If the high voltage buses are conductively isolated from each other, isolation resistance shall be measured for each electrical circuit. Moreover, modifications necessary for measuring the isolation resistance may be carried out, such as removal of the cover in order to reach the live parts, drawing of measurement lines and change in software. In cases where the measured values are not stable due to the operation of the on-board isolation resistance monitoring system, necessary modifications for conducting the measurement may be carried out by stopping the operation of the device concerned or by removing it. Furthermore, when the device is removed, a set of drawings will be used to prove that the isolation resistance between the live parts and the electrical chassis remains unchanged. These modifications shall not influence the test results. Utmost care shall be exercised to avoid short circuit and electric shock since this confirmation might require direct operations of the high-voltage circuit.

R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.1.title: Measurement method using DC voltage from external sources
R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.1.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train > Isolation resistance
R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.1.text: Measurement method using DC voltage from external sources

R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.1.1.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train > Isolation resistance > Measurement method using DC voltage from external sources
R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.1.1.text: Measurement instrument An isolation resistance test instrument capable of applying a DC voltage higher than the working voltage of the high voltage bus shall be used.

R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.1.2.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train > Isolation resistance > Measurement method using DC voltage from external sources
R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.1.2.text: Measurement method An isolation resistance test instrument is connected between the live parts and the electrical chassis. The isolation resistance is subsequently measured by applying a DC voltage at least half of the working voltage of the high voltage bus. If the system has several voltage ranges (e.g. because of boost converter) in conductively connected circuit and some of the components cannot withstand the working voltage of the entire circuit, the isolation resistance between those components and the electrical chassis can be measured separately by applying at least half of their own working voltage with those components disconnected.

R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.2.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train > Isolation resistance
R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.2.text: Measurement method using the vehicle's own REESS as DC voltage source.

R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.2.1.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train > Isolation resistance > Measurement method using DC voltage from external sources
R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.2.1.text: Test vehicle conditions The high voltage-bus is energized by the vehicle's own REESS and/or energy conversion system and the voltage level of the REESS and/or energy conversion system throughout the test shall be at least the nominal operating voltage as specified by the vehicle manufacturer.

R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.2.2.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train > Isolation resistance > Measurement method using DC voltage from external sources
R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.2.2.text: Measurement instrument The voltmeter used in this test shall measure DC values and have an internal resistance of at least 10 MΩ.

R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.2.3.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train > Isolation resistance > Measurement method using DC voltage from external sources

R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.2.3.1.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train > Isolation resistance > Measurement method using DC voltage from external sources
R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.2.3.1.text: First step The voltage is measured as shown in Figure 1 and the high voltage bus voltage (Ub) is recorded. Ub shall be equal to or greater than the nominal operating voltage of the REESS and/or energy conversion system as specified by the vehicle manufacturer.

R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.2.3.2.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train > Isolation resistance > Measurement method using DC voltage from external sources
R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.2.3.2.text: Second step The voltage (U1) between the negative side of the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis is measured and recorded (see Figure 1).

R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.2.3.3.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train > Isolation resistance > Measurement method using DC voltage from external sources
R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.2.3.3.text: Third step The voltage (U2) between the positive side of the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis is measured and recorded (see Figure 1).

R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.2.3.4.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train > Isolation resistance > Measurement method using DC voltage from external sources
R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.2.3.4.text: Fourth step If U1 is greater than or equal to U2, a standard known resistance (Ro) is inserted between the negative side of the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis. With Ro installed, the voltage (U1') between the negative side of the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis is measured (see Figure 5). The electrical isolation (Ri) is calculated according to the following formula: Ri = Ro*Ub*(1/U1' - 1/U1) Figure 5 **Measurement of U1’** If U2 is greater than U1, insert a standard known resistance (Ro) between the positive side of the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis. With Ro installed, measure the voltage (U2’) between the positive side of the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis (see Figure 6 below). The electrical isolation (Ri) is calculated according to the following formula: Ri = Ro*Ub*(1/U2’ - 1/U2) Figure 6 **Measurement of U2’**

R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.2.3.5.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train > Isolation resistance > Measurement method using DC voltage from external sources
R137|base|Annex 9 5.2.2.3.5.text: Fifth step. The electrical isolation value Ri (in Ω) divided by the working voltage of the high voltage bus (in V) results in the isolation resistance (in Ω/V). Note: The standard known resistance Ro (in Ω) should be the value of the minimum required isolation resistance (Ω/V) multiplied by the working voltage (V) of the vehicle plus/minus 20 per cent. Ro is not required to be precisely this value since the equations are valid for any Ro; however, a Ro value in this range should provide a good resolution for the voltage measurements.

R137|base|Annex 9 6.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train
R137|base|Annex 9 6.text: Electrolyte leakage An appropriate coating, if necessary, may be applied to the physical protection (casing) in order to confirm if there is any electrolyte leakage from the REESS resulting from the test. Unless the manufacturer provides means to differentiate between the leakage of different liquids, all liquid leakage shall be considered as the electrolyte.

R137|base|Annex 9 7.heading: Annex 9 Test Procedures for vehicles equipped with the electric power train
R137|base|Annex 9 7.text: REESS retention Compliance shall be determined by visual inspection.

R137|base|3.1.heading: Application for approval
R137|base|3.1.text: The application for approval of a vehicle type with regard to the protection of the occupants of the front seats in the event of a frontal collision shall be submitted by the vehicle manufacturer or by their duly accredited representative.

R137|base|3.2.heading: Application for approval
R137|base|3.2.text: It shall be accompanied by the undermentioned documents in triplicate and following particulars:

R137|base|3.2.1.heading: Application for approval
R137|base|3.2.1.text: A detailed description of the vehicle type with respect to its structure, dimensions, lines and constituent materials;

R137|base|3.2.2.heading: Application for approval
R137|base|3.2.2.text: Photographs, and/or diagrams and drawings of the vehicle showing the vehicle type in front, side and rear elevation and design details of the forward part of the structure;

R137|base|3.2.3.heading: Application for approval
R137|base|3.2.3.text: Particulars of the vehicle's unladen kerb mass;

R137|base|3.2.4.heading: Application for approval
R137|base|3.2.4.text: The lines and inside dimensions of the passenger compartment;

R137|base|3.2.5.heading: Application for approval
R137|base|3.2.5.text: A description of the interior fittings and protective systems installed in the vehicle;

R137|base|3.2.6.heading: Application for approval
R137|base|3.2.6.text: A general description of the electrical power source type, location and the electric power train (e.g. hybrid, electric).

R137|base|3.3.heading: Application for approval
R137|base|3.3.text: The applicant for approval shall be entitled to present any data and results of tests carried out which make it possible to establish that compliance with the requirements can be achieved with a sufficient degree of confidence.

R137|base|3.4.heading: Application for approval
R137|base|3.4.text: A vehicle which is representative of the type to be approved shall be submitted to the Technical Service responsible for conducting the approval tests.

R137|base|3.4.1.heading: Application for approval
R137|base|3.4.1.text: A vehicle not comprising all the components proper to the type may be accepted for test provided that it can be shown that the absence of the components has no detrimental effect on the results of the test in so far as the requirements of this Regulation are concerned.

R137|base|3.4.2.heading: Application for approval
R137|base|3.4.2.text: It shall be the responsibility of the applicant for approval to show that the application of paragraph 3.4.1. above is compatible with compliance with the requirements of this Regulation.

R137|base|Annex 5 1.title: Arrangement of dummies
R137|base|Annex 5 1.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems

R137|base|Annex 5 1.1.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Arrangement of dummies
R137|base|Annex 5 1.1.text: Separate seats The plane of symmetry of the dummy shall coincide with the vertical median plane of the seat.

R137|base|Annex 5 1.2.title: Front bench seat
R137|base|Annex 5 1.2.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Arrangement of dummies

R137|base|Annex 5 1.2.1.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Arrangement of dummies > Front bench seat
R137|base|Annex 5 1.2.1.text: Driver The plane of symmetry of the dummy shall lie in the vertical plane passing through the steering wheel centre and parallel to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle. If the seating position is determined by the shape of the bench, such seat shall be regarded as a separate seat.

R137|base|Annex 5 1.2.2.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Arrangement of dummies > Front bench seat
R137|base|Annex 5 1.2.2.text: Outer passenger The plane of symmetry of the dummy shall be symmetrical with that of the driver dummy relative to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle. If the seating position is determined by the shape of the bench, such seat shall be regarded as a separate seat.

R137|base|Annex 5 1.3.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Arrangement of dummies
R137|base|Annex 5 1.3.text: Bench seat for front passengers (not including driver) The planes of symmetry of the dummy shall coincide with the median planes of the seating positions defined by the manufacturer.

R137|base|Annex 5 2.title: Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat
R137|base|Annex 5 2.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems
R137|base|Annex 5 2.text: Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat

R137|base|Annex 5 2.1.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat
R137|base|Annex 5 2.1.text: Head The transverse instrumentation platform of the head shall be horizontal within 2.5°. To level the head of the test dummy in vehicles with upright seats with non-adjustable backs, the following sequences shall be followed. First adjust the position of the "H" point within the limits set forth in paragraph 2.4.3.1. below to level the transverse instrumentation platform of the head of the test dummy. If the transverse instrumentation platform of the head is still not level, then adjust the pelvic angle of the test dummy within the limits provided in paragraph 2.4.3.2. below. If the transverse instrumentation platform of the head is still not level, then adjust the neck bracket of the test dummy the minimum amount necessary to ensure that the transverse instrumentation platform of the head is horizontal within 2.5°.

R137|base|Annex 5 2.2.title: Arms
R137|base|Annex 5 2.2.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat

R137|base|Annex 5 2.2.1.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Arms
R137|base|Annex 5 2.2.1.text: The driver's upper arms shall be adjacent to the torso with the centrelines as close to a vertical plane as possible.

R137|base|Annex 5 2.3.title: Hands
R137|base|Annex 5 2.3.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat

R137|base|Annex 5 2.3.1.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Hands
R137|base|Annex 5 2.3.1.text: The palms of the driver test dummy shall be in contact with the outer part of the steering wheel rim at the rim's horizontal centreline. The thumbs shall be over the steering wheel rim and shall be lightly taped to the steering wheel rim so that if the hand of the test dummy is pushed upward by a force of not less than 9 N and not more than 22 N, the tape shall release the hand from the steering wheel rim.

R137|base|Annex 5 2.4.title: Torso
R137|base|Annex 5 2.4.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat

R137|base|Annex 5 2.4.1.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Torso
R137|base|Annex 5 2.4.1.text: In vehicles equipped with bench seats, the upper torso of the driver test dummy shall rest against the seat back. The midsagittal plane of the driver dummy shall be vertical and parallel to the vehicle's longitudinal centreline, and pass through the centre of the steering wheel rim.

R137|base|Annex 5 2.4.2.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Torso
R137|base|Annex 5 2.4.2.text: In vehicles equipped with individual seats, the upper torso of the driver test dummy shall rest against the seat back. The midsagittal plane of the driver dummy shall be vertical and shall coincide with the longitudinal centreline of the individual seat.

R137|base|Annex 5 2.4.3.title: Lower torso
R137|base|Annex 5 2.4.3.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Torso

R137|base|Annex 5 2.4.3.1.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Torso > Lower torso
R137|base|Annex 5 2.4.3.1.text: "H" point The "H" point of the driver test dummy shall coincide within 13 mm in the vertical dimension and 13 mm in the horizontal dimension, with a point 6 mm below the position of the "H" point determined using the procedure described in Annex 6 except that the length of the lower leg and thigh segments of the "H" point machine shall be adjusted to 414 and 401 mm, instead of 417 and 432 mm respectively.

R137|base|Annex 5 2.4.3.2.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Torso > Lower torso
R137|base|Annex 5 2.4.3.2.text: Pelvic angle As determined using the pelvic angle gauge (GM) drawing 78051-532 incorporated by reference in Part 572 which is inserted into the "H" point gauging hole of the dummy, the angle measured from the horizontal on the 76.2 mm (3 inch) flat surface of the gauge shall be 22.5 degrees plus or minus 2.5 degrees.

R137|base|Annex 5 2.5.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat
R137|base|Annex 5 2.5.text: Legs The upper legs of the driver test dummy shall rest against the seat cushion to the extent permitted by placement of the feet. The initial distance between the outboard knee clevis flange surfaces shall be 270 mm ± 10 mm. To the extent practicable, the left leg of the driver dummy shall be in vertical longitudinal planes. To the extent practicable, the right leg of the driver dummy shall be in a vertical plane. Final adjustment to accommodate placement of feet in accordance with paragraph 2.6. for various passenger compartment configurations is permitted.

R137|base|Annex 5 2.6.title: Feet
R137|base|Annex 5 2.6.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat

R137|base|Annex 5 2.6.1.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Feet
R137|base|Annex 5 2.6.1.text: The right foot of the driver test dummy shall rest on the undepressed accelerator with the rearmost point of the heel on the floor surface in the plane of the pedal. If the foot cannot be placed on the accelerator pedal, it shall be positioned perpendicular to the tibia and placed as far forward as possible in the direction of the centreline of the pedal with the rearmost point of the heel resting on the floor surface. The heel of the left foot shall be placed as far forward as possible and shall rest on the floor pan. The left foot shall be positioned as flat as possible on the toe board. The longitudinal centreline of the left foot shall be placed as parallel as possible to the longitudinal centreline of the vehicle. For vehicles equipped with a footrest, it shall be possible at the request of the manufacturer to place the left foot on the footrest. In this case the position of the left foot is defined by the footrest.

R137|base|Annex 5 2.7.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat
R137|base|Annex 5 2.7.text: The measuring instruments installed shall not in any way affect the movement of the dummy during impact.

R137|base|Annex 5 2.8.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat
R137|base|Annex 5 2.8.text: The temperature of the dummy and the system of measuring instruments shall be stabilized before the test and maintained so far as possible within a range between 19 °C and 22.2 °C.

R137|base|Annex 5 2.9.title: Dummy HIII fiftieth percentile clothing
R137|base|Annex 5 2.9.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat

R137|base|Annex 5 2.9.1.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Dummy HIII fiftieth percentile clothing
R137|base|Annex 5 2.9.1.text: The instrumented dummy will be clothed in formfitting cotton stretch garments with short sleeves and midcalf length trousers specified in FMVSS 208, drawings 78051-292 and 293 or their equivalent.

R137|base|Annex 5 2.9.2.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Dummy HIII fiftieth percentile clothing
R137|base|Annex 5 2.9.2.text: A size 11XW shoe, which meets the configuration size, sole and heel thickness specifications of the United States of America military standard MIL S 13192, revision P and whose weight is 0.57 ± 0.1 kg, shall be placed and fastened on each foot of the test dummy.

R137|base|Annex 5 3.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems
R137|base|Annex 5 3.text: Installation of the dummy Hybrid III fifth percentile female dummy on the passenger seat. The longitudinal and vertical dimension of "H" point are described as (X50thM, Z50thM) and the longitudinal and vertical dimension of "H 5th " point are described as (X5thF, Z5thF). XSCL is defined as the horizontal distance between the "H" point and the most forward point on the seat cushion (see Fig. 1). Use the following formula to calculate the "H 5th " point. Note that X5thF should always be more forward than the X50thM. X5thF = X50thM, + (93mm - 0.323 x XSCL) Z5thF = Z50thM Figure 1

R137|base|Annex 5 3.1.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat
R137|base|Annex 5 3.1.text: Head The transverse instrumentation platform of the head shall be horizontal within 2.5°.

R137|base|Annex 5 3.1.1.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Dummy HIII fiftieth percentile clothing
R137|base|Annex 5 3.1.1.text: To level the head of the test dummy in vehicles with upright seats with non-adjustable backs, the following sequences shall be followed. First adjust the position of the "H 5th " point within the limits set forth in paragraph 3.4.3.1. below to level the transverse instrumentation platform of the head of the test dummy. If the transverse instrumentation platform of the head is still not level, then adjust the pelvic angle of the test dummy within the limits provided in paragraph 3.4.3.2. below. If the transverse instrumentation platform of the head is still not level, then adjust the neck bracket of the test dummy to the minimum amount necessary to ensure that the transverse instrumentation platform of the head is horizontal within 2.5°.

R137|base|Annex 5 3.1.2.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Dummy HIII fiftieth percentile clothing
R137|base|Annex 5 3.1.2.text: To level the head of the test dummy in vehicles with adjustable backs, the following sequences shall be followed. First adjust the position of the "H 5th " point within the limits set forth in paragraph 3.4.3.1. below to level the transverse instrumentation platform of the head of the test dummy. If the transverse instrumentation platform of the head is still not level, then adjust the pelvic angle of the test dummy within the limits provided in paragraph 3.4.3.2. below. If the transverse instrumentation platform of the head is still not level, then adjust the neck bracket of the test dummy to the minimum amount necessary to ensure that the transverse instrumentation platform of the head is horizontal within 2.5°. If the transverse instrumentation platform of the head is still not level, then adjust the seat back to a different angle at a minimum amount necessary to ensure that the transverse instrumentation platform of the head is horizontal within 2.5°.

R137|base|Annex 5 3.2.title: Arms
R137|base|Annex 5 3.2.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat

R137|base|Annex 5 3.2.1.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Arms
R137|base|Annex 5 3.2.1.text: The passenger's upper arms shall be in contact with the seat back and the sides of the torso.

R137|base|Annex 5 3.3.title: Hands
R137|base|Annex 5 3.3.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat

R137|base|Annex 5 3.3.1.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Hands
R137|base|Annex 5 3.3.1.text: The palms of the passenger test dummy shall be in contact with outside of thigh. The little finger shall be in contact with the seat cushion.

R137|base|Annex 5 3.4.title: Torso
R137|base|Annex 5 3.4.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat

R137|base|Annex 5 3.4.1.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Torso
R137|base|Annex 5 3.4.1.text: In vehicles equipped with bench seats, the upper torso of the passenger test dummy shall rest against the seat back. The midsagittal plane of the passenger dummy shall be vertical and parallel to the vehicle's longitudinal centreline and the same distance from the vehicle's longitudinal centreline as the midsagittal plane of the driver dummy.

R137|base|Annex 5 3.4.2.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Torso
R137|base|Annex 5 3.4.2.text: In vehicles equipped with individual seats, the upper torso of the passenger test dummy shall rest against the seat back. The midsagittal plane of the passenger dummy shall be vertical and shall coincide with the longitudinal centreline of the individual seat.

R137|base|Annex 5 3.4.3.title: Lower torso
R137|base|Annex 5 3.4.3.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Torso

R137|base|Annex 5 3.4.3.1.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Torso > Lower torso
R137|base|Annex 5 3.4.3.1.text: "H 5th " point The "H 5th " point of passenger test dummy shall coincide within 13 mm in the horizontal dimension, of the "H 5th " point determined using the procedure described in Annex 6 and paragraph 3 above.

R137|base|Annex 5 3.4.3.2.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Torso > Lower torso
R137|base|Annex 5 3.4.3.2.text: Pelvic angle As determined using the pelvic angle gauge (GM) drawing 78051-532 incorporated by reference in Part 572 which is inserted into the "H" point gauging hole of the dummy, the angle measured from the horizontal on the 76.2 mm (3 inch) flat surface of the gauge shall be 20 degrees plus or minus 2.5 degrees.

R137|base|Annex 5 3.5.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat
R137|base|Annex 5 3.5.text: Legs The upper legs of the passenger test dummy shall rest against the seat cushion to the extent permitted by placement of the feet. The initial distance between the outboard knee clevis flange surfaces shall be 229 mm ± 5 mm as shown in Figure 2. To the extent practicable, both legs of the passenger dummy shall be in vertical longitudinal planes. Final adjustment to accommodate placement of feet in accordance with paragraph 3.6. for various passenger compartment configurations is permitted. Figure 2 **The initial knee distance of Hybrid III fifth percentile female**

R137|base|Annex 5 3.6.title: Feet
R137|base|Annex 5 3.6.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat

R137|base|Annex 5 3.6.1.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Feet
R137|base|Annex 5 3.6.1.text: The legs shall be positioned as distant as possible from the front end of the seat cushion while the thighs are kept in contact with the seat cushion as shown in Fig.(a). As shown in Fig.(b), each leg shall be lowered until the foot comes in contact with the floor while the foot and tibia are kept in a right angle to one another and the thigh inclination angle kept constant. When each heel is in contact with the floor, the foot shall be rotated so that the toe comes as much in contact as possible with the floor as shown in Fig.(c). If it is not possible to have each foot in contact with the floor, the foot shall be lowered until the calf comes in contact with the front end of the seat cushion or the back of the foot comes in contact with the vehicle interior. The foot shall be kept as parallel as possible to the floor as shown in Fig.(d). In case of interference from a vehicle body protrusion, the foot shall be rotated as minimally as possible around the tibia. In case interference still remains, the femur shall be rotated to resolve or minimize the interference. The foot shall be moved inward or outward while the separation distance between the knees is kept constant. <!-- Start of picture text --> Figure (a) Figure (b) Figure (c) Figure (d) [figure not available] <!-- End of picture text -->

R137|base|Annex 5 3.7.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat
R137|base|Annex 5 3.7.text: The measuring instruments installed shall not in any way affect the movement of the dummy during impact.

R137|base|Annex 5 3.8.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat
R137|base|Annex 5 3.8.text: The temperature of the dummies and the system of measuring instruments shall be stabilized before the test and maintained so far as possible within a range between 19 °C and 22.2 °C.

R137|base|Annex 5 3.9.title: Dummy HIII fifth percentile clothing
R137|base|Annex 5 3.9.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat

R137|base|Annex 5 3.9.1.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Dummy HIII fifth percentile clothing
R137|base|Annex 5 3.9.1.text: The instrumented dummy will be clothed in formfitting cotton stretch garments with short sleeves and midcalf length trousers specified in FMVSS 208, drawings 78051-292 and 293 or their equivalent.

R137|base|Annex 5 3.9.2.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems > Installation of the dummy HIII fiftieth percentile on the driver seat > Dummy HIII fifth percentile clothing
R137|base|Annex 5 3.9.2.text: A size 7.5 W small female size shoe, which meets the configuration size, sole and heel thickness specifications of the United States of America military standard MIL-S-21711E, revision P and whose weight is 0.41 ± 0.09 kg, shall be placed and fastened on each foot of the test dummies.

R137|base|Annex 5 4.heading: Annex 5 Arrangement and installation of dummies and adjustment of restraint systems
R137|base|Annex 5 4.text: Adjustment of restraint system The dummy jacket shall be installed at the appropriate position where the bolt hole of the neck lower bracket and the work hole of the dummy jacket should be at the same position. With the test dummy at its designated seating position as specified by the appropriate requirements of paragraphs 2.1. through 2.6. and paragraphs 3.1 to 3.6 above, place the belt around the test dummy and fasten the latch. Remove all slack from the lap belt. Pull the upper torso webbing out of the retractor and allow it to retract. Repeat this operation four times. The shoulder belt should be at the position between the area which shall not be taken off of shoulder and shall not come in contact with the neck. The seat belt path shall be positioned: for Hybrid III fiftieth percentile male dummy, the hole of the outer side dummy jacket shall not be fully hidden by the seat belt. For Hybrid III fifth percentile female dummy, the seat belt shall lie between the breasts. Apply a 9 to 18 N tension load to the lap belt. If the belt system is equipped with a tension-relieving device, introduce the maximum amount of slack into the upper torso belt that is recommended by the manufacturer for normal use in the owner's manual for the vehicle. If the belt system is not equipped with a tension-relieving device, allow the excess webbing in the shoulder belt to be retracted by the rewind force of the retractor. Where the safety belt and safety belt anchorages are located such that the belt does not lie as required above then the safety belt may be manually adjusted and retained by tape.

R137|base|Annex 7 1.1.heading: Annex 7 Test procedure with trolley > Test installation and procedure
R137|base|Annex 7 1.1.text: Trolley The trolley shall be so constructed that no permanent deformation appears after the test. It shall be so guided that, during the impact phase, the deviation in the vertical plane does not exceed 5° and 2° in the horizontal plane.

R137|base|Annex 7 1.2.title: State of the structure
R137|base|Annex 7 1.2.heading: Annex 7 Test procedure with trolley > Test installation and procedure

R137|base|Annex 7 1.2.1.heading: Annex 7 Test procedure with trolley > Test installation and procedure > State of the structure
R137|base|Annex 7 1.2.1.text: General The structure tested shall be representative of the series production of the vehicles concerned. Some components may be replaced or removed where such replacement or removal clearly has no effect on the test results.

R137|base|Annex 7 1.2.2.heading: Annex 7 Test procedure with trolley > Test installation and procedure > State of the structure
R137|base|Annex 7 1.2.2.text: Adjustments Adjustments shall conform to those set out in paragraph 1.4.3. of Annex 3 to this Regulation, taking into account what is stated in paragraph 1.2.1. above.

R137|base|Annex 7 1.3.title: Attachment of the structure
R137|base|Annex 7 1.3.heading: Annex 7 Test procedure with trolley > Test installation and procedure

R137|base|Annex 7 1.3.1.heading: Annex 7 Test procedure with trolley > Test installation and procedure > Attachment of the structure
R137|base|Annex 7 1.3.1.text: The structure shall be firmly attached to the trolley in such a way that no relative displacement occurs during the test.

R137|base|Annex 7 1.3.2.heading: Annex 7 Test procedure with trolley > Test installation and procedure > Attachment of the structure
R137|base|Annex 7 1.3.2.text: The method used to fasten the structure to the trolley shall not have the effect of strengthening the seat anchorages or restraint devices, or of producing any abnormal deformation of the structure.

R137|base|Annex 7 1.3.3.heading: Annex 7 Test procedure with trolley > Test installation and procedure > Attachment of the structure
R137|base|Annex 7 1.3.3.text: The attachment device recommended is that whereby the structure rests on supports placed approximately in the axis of the wheels or, if possible, whereby the structure is secured to the trolley by the fastenings of the suspension system.

R137|base|Annex 7 1.3.4.heading: Annex 7 Test procedure with trolley > Test installation and procedure > Attachment of the structure
R137|base|Annex 7 1.3.4.text: The angle between the longitudinal axis of the vehicle and the direction of motion of the trolley shall be 0° ± 2°.

R137|base|Annex 7 1.4.heading: Annex 7 Test procedure with trolley > Test installation and procedure
R137|base|Annex 7 1.4.text: Dummies The dummies and their positioning shall conform to the specifications in Annex 3, paragraph 2.

R137|base|Annex 7 1.5.title: Measuring apparatus
R137|base|Annex 7 1.5.heading: Annex 7 Test procedure with trolley > Test installation and procedure

R137|base|Annex 7 1.5.1.heading: Annex 7 Test procedure with trolley > Test installation and procedure > Measuring apparatus
R137|base|Annex 7 1.5.1.text: Deceleration of the structure The position of the transducers measuring the deceleration of the structure during the impact shall be parallel to the longitudinal axis of the trolley according to the specifications of Annex 8 (CFC 180).

R137|base|Annex 7 1.5.2.heading: Annex 7 Test procedure with trolley > Test installation and procedure > Measuring apparatus
R137|base|Annex 7 1.5.2.text: Measurements to be made on the dummies All the measurements necessary for checking the listed criteria are set out in Annex 3, paragraph 5.

R137|base|Annex 7 1.6.heading: Annex 7 Test procedure with trolley > Test installation and procedure
R137|base|Annex 7 1.6.text: Deceleration curve of the structure The deceleration curve of the structure during the impact phase shall be such that the "variation of speed in relation to time" curve obtained by integration at no point differs by more than ±1 m/s from the "variation of speed in relation to time" reference curve of the vehicle concerned as defined in appendix to this annex. A displacement with regard to the time axis of the reference curve may be used to obtain the structure velocity inside the corridor.

R137|base|Annex 7 1.7.heading: Annex 7 Test procedure with trolley > Test installation and procedure
R137|base|Annex 7 1.7.text: Reference curve ∆V = f(t) of the vehicle concerned This reference curve is obtained by integration of the deceleration curve of the vehicle concerned measured in the frontal collision test against a barrier as provided for in paragraph 6. of Annex 3 to this Regulation.

R137|base|Annex 7 1.8.heading: Annex 7 Test procedure with trolley > Test installation and procedure
R137|base|Annex 7 1.8.text: Equivalent method The test may be performed by some other method than that of deceleration of a trolley, provided that such method complies with the requirement concerning the range of variation of speed described in paragraph 1.6. above.

R137|base|12.1.heading: Transitional provisions
R137|base|12.1.text: As from the official date of entry into force of the 03 series of amendments, no Contracting Party applying this UN Regulation shall refuse to grant or refuse to accept type-approvals under this UN Regulation as amended by the 03 series of amendments.

R137|base|12.2.heading: Transitional provisions
R137|base|12.2.text: As from 1 September 2027, Contracting Parties applying this UN Regulation shall not be obliged to accept type-approvals of vehicles according to the preceding series of amendments, first issued after 1 September 2027.

R137|base|12.3.heading: Transitional provisions
R137|base|12.3.text: Contracting Parties applying this UN Regulation shall continue to accept type-approvals of vehicles according to the preceding series of amendments, first issued before 1 September 2027 provided the transitional provisions in these respective previous series of amendments foresee this possibility.

R137|base|12.4.heading: Transitional provisions
R137|base|12.4.text: Contracting Parties applying this UN Regulation may grant type-approvals according to any preceding series of amendments to this UN Regulation.

R137|base|12.5.heading: Transitional provisions

R137|base|12.6.heading: Transitional provisions
R137|base|12.6.text: Notwithstanding the transitional provisions above, Contracting Parties who start to apply this Regulation after the date of entry into force of the most recent series of amendments are not obliged to accept type-approvals which were granted in accordance with any of the preceding series of amendments to this Regulation.
